item.description: $12.99 for a 12 pack of Sprite in North San Diego is wild. That is basically $1.08 per can before tax or CRV. And yeah, the digital coupon drops it to $4.99, but only if you buy 5 or more. That is the part that annoys me. The “normal” price is insane, then suddenly the store can knock $8 off if you agree to buy a small warehouse worth of soda. So apparently the real price is somewhere between “reasonable” and “absolutely not,” depending on whether you are willing to stockpile it. This is why grocery shopping feels like a game now. Regular price. Member price. Digital coupon. Buy 5. Mix and match. Scan the app. Meanwhile I just wanted one case of Sprite.

item.title: GovBrief Today #586
item.description: A Border Patrol analyst in Spokane read a stranger's bank activity, and a Montana trooper found a reason to pull him over. Nobody knows how a federal agent in Washington and a state trooper in Montana came to be talking about one black Chevy on Interstate 90, because the government won't say. We know it happened only because the paperwork surfaced in his court case. The analyst's memo says he saw "financial activity patterns" in federal databases and put the car out as a lookout. On bodycam, the trooper told the driver it was "nothing major," just a plate cover. The Spokane unit is called the Predictive Intelligence Targeting Team, and true to its name, it exists to predict whether you might be doing something illegal. Customs and Border Protection will not say what financial records it reads, whether a warrant is involved, or how many of its 20 sectors participate. In Texas the same program had a deputy search a driver's truck on a lane-drift stop and find nothing. That driver was never charged. I've emailed 9,011 stories over 586 straight nights, free and without ads. The algorithm can't show them all to you. Add your email address at govbrief.today and I will. item.title: He tried his best to build an accessible guitar
item.description: Asfvision is Anthony S. Ferraro, he advocates for less sighted people by doing skateboarding, sports, and arts. Nvision guitars specializes in building custom guitars for people with less sight, including tactile fret markers, textured knobs, and ergonomic bodies. https://nvisionguitarsllc.square.site/ By engineering for those with less abilities and resources, we end up finding universal aids that help everyone. As a guitarist, I know many of us would love tactile necks to not look down as much, if we play live in the dark, and just to learn without visually checking which frets we are on. Not an ad, no association with either party in this video, just sharing the love
